# Proverbs 28 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Guilty people run even when nobody's chasing them, but the righteous are as fearless as a lion.

**2** When a nation sins, it cycles through one leader after another — but a wise, knowledgeable leader brings stability.

**3** A poor person who exploits other poor people is like a driving rain that destroys the crops — devastating and pointless.

**4** People who abandon God's instruction end up applauding the wicked, but those who follow it stand up and fight them.

**5** Evil people don't understand justice at all, but people who seek the LORD understand it perfectly.

**6** Better to be poor and honest than rich and crooked.

**7** A child who obeys their parents' teaching shows real understanding, but one who hangs out with the wrong crowd humiliates their father.

**8** If you build wealth through excessive interest, someone who's generous to the poor will end up with it instead.

**9** If you refuse to listen to God's instruction, even your prayers become offensive to Him.

**10** Lead honest people down a wrong path and you'll fall into your own trap — but the blameless will inherit what's good.

**11** Rich people often think they know everything, but a poor person with discernment can see right through them.

**12** When good people are in charge, everyone celebrates. When the wicked take power, people go into hiding.

**13** Hide your sins and you'll never succeed. Confess them and leave them behind, and you'll receive mercy.

**14** Blessed is the person who maintains a healthy sense of reverence, but those who harden their hearts will fall into disaster.

**15** A corrupt leader over a vulnerable people is as terrifying as a roaring lion or a charging bear.

**16** A leader without wisdom is a brutal tyrant, but one who hates corruption will have a long reign.

**17** Anyone guilty of murder will be a fugitive until death — don't help them escape.

**18** Live with integrity and you'll be kept safe. Live a double life and you'll eventually collapse.

**19** Farm your land and you'll have plenty. Chase fantasies and you'll have plenty of nothing.

**20** A faithful person overflows with blessings, but anyone trying to get rich quick will get what's coming to them.

**21** Favoritism is wrong — and some people will compromise their integrity for something as cheap as a piece of bread.

**22** A greedy person chases money and doesn't realize that poverty is on its way.

**23** Honest correction earns more lasting respect than smooth flattery.

**24** Stealing from your parents and calling it 'no big deal' makes you no different from a destroyer.

**25** Selfish ambition starts fights, but trusting the LORD leads to prosperity.

**26** Trusting your own instincts makes you a fool. Walking in wisdom is what keeps you safe.

**27** Give to the poor and you'll never lack. Look the other way and you'll be cursed.

**28** When wicked people gain power, everyone hides. When they're gone, the righteous flourish again.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **28:1**: Guilt is its own punishment — it makes you run from shadows. Integrity gives you the courage of a lion.

- **28:13**: One of the most important verses in the Bible on repentance — hiding your mistakes leads nowhere; confessing and changing direction leads to mercy.

- **28:27**: The generosity principle again — giving to the poor doesn't make you poorer; it ensures you won't lack. Ignoring the poor invites curses.

— PNEUMA
